message.abstract: <jats:p>In Barendregt (1984), Corrado Böhm conjectured that every adequate (Barendregt 1984, 6.4.2 (ii)) numeral system of normal combinators has normal successor, predecessor and zero test. In this note, we give a counterexample to this conjecture. Our example is shown to have no normal zero test. Böhm has informed us that Intrigila (1994) has given an example with no normal successor. Our strategy, in terms of the <jats:bold>ant-lion paradigm</jats:bold>, is to pry open the trap so wide that it enters its active state before its jaws are shut.</jats:p>
title: Taming the wild ant-lion; a counterexample to a conjecture of Böhm

message.abstract: <jats:title>Abstract</jats:title><jats:p>We consider three problems concerning alpha conversion of closed terms (combinators).</jats:p><jats:p>(1) Given a combinator <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> find the an alpha convert of <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> with a smallest number of distinct variables.</jats:p><jats:p>(2) Given two alpha convertible combinators <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> find a shortest alpha conversion of <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> to <jats:italic>N</jats:italic>.</jats:p><jats:p>(3) Given two alpha convertible combinators <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> find an alpha conversion of <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> to <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> which uses the smallest number of variables possible along the way.</jats:p><jats:p>We obtain the following results.</jats:p><jats:p>(1) There is a polynomial time algorithm for solving problem (1). It is reducible to vertex coloring of chordal graphs.</jats:p><jats:p>(2) Problem (2) is <jats:italic>co-NP</jats:italic> complete (in recognition form). The general feedback vertex set problem for digraphs is reducible to problem (2).</jats:p><jats:p>(3) At most one variable besides those occurring in both <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> and <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> is necessary. This appears to be the folklore but the proof is not familiar. A polynomial time algorithm for the alpha conversion of <jats:italic>M</jats:italic> to <jats:italic>N</jats:italic> using at most one extra variable is given.</jats:p><jats:p>There is a tradeoff between solutions to problem (2) and problem (3) which we do not fully understand.</jats:p>
title: On the complexity of alpha conversion
On the Structure of Armstrong Relations for Functional Dependencies

message.abstract: <jats:p>In [4] Gordon Plotkin considers the problem of characterizing the <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>-definable functionals in full type structures. A plausible, but, as we shall see, quite false, conjecture is that a functional is <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>-definable ⇔ it is invariant in the sense of Fraenkel and Mostowski. A better guess might be that the set of <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>-definable functionals of type <jats:italic>σ</jats:italic> has a uniform (in <jats:italic>σ</jats:italic>) definition in type theory over all full type structures (Plotkin explicitly considers a certain sort of definition by means of “logical relations”). More or less generally, one may ask if the following question is decidable.</jats:p><jats:p>Given: a functional <jats:italic>F</jats:italic> in a full type structure over a finite ground domain.</jats:p><jats:p>Question: is <jats:italic>F</jats:italic><jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>-definable?</jats:p><jats:p>We call the statement that this question is decidable Plotkin's <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>-definability conjecture. We do not know if Plotkin's conjecture is true.</jats:p><jats:p>In this note we consider several questions which quickly arise from Plotkin's conjecture. In <jats:italic>§</jats:italic>1, we ask which type structures satisfy <jats:italic>λ</jats:italic>-definability = invariance. We construct for each consistent set of equations a model satisfying this equality. From consideration of these models we obtain a number of syntactic corollaries including a reduction of <jats:italic>βη</jats:italic>-conversion to <jats:italic>βη</jats:italic>-conversion at a single type (Theorem 3), an “<jats:italic>ω</jats:italic>-rule” for <jats:italic>βη</jats:italic>-conversion (Proposition 6) and consistency with <jats:italic>βη</jats:italic>-conversion (Proposition 8), definability and indefinability results for versions of Kronecker's <jats:italic>δ</jats:italic> (Propositions 10 and 11), and a decidability result for the problem of inter-definability among combinators.</jats:p>
title: Completeness, invariance and λ-definability
Reductions of the graph reconstruction conjecture
